name: Foxglove
family: Plantaginaceae, the plantain family (once placed in the figwort family)
grown_as: The wild foxglove, a biennial: a rosette of leaves in the first year, a tall flower spike in the second, then it dies after seeding. William's library also has the variety 'Dalmatian Peach', which flowers in its first year, is shorter (60 to 90 cm) and has soft peach-pink flowers. Drawn as the wild purple-pink foxglove. ⚠️ CHECK which one to draw.
habit: First year: a flat rosette of soft leaves about 30 to 50 cm across. Second year: one stiff, unbranched, downy stem 1 to 1.5 m tall (up to 2 m), leafy low down, carrying a long spike of hanging bells over its top half.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base, then alternate up the stem, getting smaller towards the spike
leaf.outline: Long oval to lance-shaped, 10 to 30 cm long, widest a little below the middle
leaf.base: Narrows gradually into a winged stalk
leaf.margin: Small, rounded, shallow teeth (scalloped) all the way round, fading out near the base
leaf.veins: A pale midrib and a fine network of veins pressed in from above, raised below, so the leaf looks quilted
leaf.surface: Soft and finely downy above; grey and woolly beneath
leaf.stalk: Rosette leaves on a broad winged stalk a third to half the length of the blade; upper stem leaves stalkless
leaf.colour: Mid to slightly greyish green above, much greyer beneath

flower.form: A hanging tubular bell like the finger of a glove, wide-mouthed and slightly flattened, the lower lip longer than the upper
flower.petals: Five petals joined into one tube; the mouth has a short upper lip and a longer lower lip with three shallow rounded lobes
flower.colour: Pinkish purple outside; paler inside, the floor of the tube spotted dark purple, each spot ringed with white, with long white hairs among the spots
flower.centre: Four cream stamens lie against the top of the tube, hidden from the side
flower.behind: Five small pointed green sepals at the base of the bell
flower.carried: In a long one-sided spike, the bells hanging down and all facing the same way; they open from the bottom of the spike upwards, so open bells sit below tight green buds at the top

fruit: An egg-shaped, pointed capsule about 1 cm long, held up the old spike with the sepals still at its base; green, ripening brown and splitting in two. Seeds tiny (under 1 mm), oblong, brown, like dust, thousands to a plant.
seedling: Two tiny round-oval seed leaves on short stalks, then oval, softly hairy true leaves with small rounded teeth, soon lying flat as a small rosette
winter: The first-year rosette stays green through winter. After flowering in the second year the plant dies; the brown dead spike can stand into winter.

leaf: long oval leaf narrowing into a winged stalk
small rounded teeth all along the edge
netted veins pressed in so the surface looks quilted
bloom: a hanging tubular bell, not an open flat flower
longer lower lip with dark spots ringed white inside
seed: tiny brown oblong seeds like dust, many together
seedling: first true leaves oval and downy, lying flat
young: a flat rosette of soft, quilted, grey-green leaves on winged stalks
flower: one tall upright stem with a long one-sided spike of hanging bells
open bells low down, green buds at the top
rosette leaves at the base, smaller leaves up the stem
seedhead: a tall brown stalk lined with pointed egg-shaped capsules
capsules held upright, split at the tip

look_alikes: Comfrey leaves can be taken for foxglove rosettes (a known poisoning risk): comfrey leaves are rough and bristly rather than soft and have no scalloped teeth. Great mullein rosettes are thicker and woolly on both sides with no teeth. Primrose leaves are smaller and stalkless. Garden foxgloves (Digitalis × mertonensis, D. grandiflora) differ in colour.
